newsitem.title: USA: Dell stock jumps after strong earnings report.
newsitem.headline: Dell stock jumps after strong earnings report.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp. stock jumped in heavy trading Wednesday, a day after the personal computer maker reported surprisingly robust quarterly profits, in a rise supported by a chorus of bullish calls by Wall Street analysts.
Dell stock climbed $2.25 to $74.375 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market. It was the most active Nasdaq stock of the day, with more than 12 million shares traded.

After the market closed Tuesday night, the mail-order of personal computer company released fourth-quarter earnings of $188 million, or $1.01 a share, vs. 1995 quarterly earnings of $70 million, or 35 cents a share.
The results eclipsed industry analysts' consensus prediction of 83 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst forecasts.
Revenues for the quarter ended Feb. 2 rose to $2.41 billion from $1.54 billion a year ago, Dell said.

The stock of Round Rock, Texas-based Dell managed to remain higher despite a sharp, broad sell-off in U.S. stocks triggered by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments before a Senate committee that the market's rise may be "unsustainable."
"Yet again, Dell blew away Street expectations, delivering $1.01 vs. our 83-cent estimate," Lehman Bros. analyst Kimberly Alexy said in the brokerage's morning meeting notes.
Contrary to expectations, the surprisingly high earnings were driven by growth in revenues, not profit margin, Alexy said.
Lehman continues to rate the stock an "outperform," and Alexy raised the earnings forecast for 1998.
Salomon Bros. analysts John Dean and Michele Rothacher said in a research note that the company "has executed flawlessly during the past year."
"The company has clearly taken maximum advantage of the benefits of the direct (sales) channel," they said.

"While we applaud Dell's flawless performance during the past year, we feel that this performance is reflected in the current price of the shares, and we maintain our 'hold' (recommendation)," they added.
Among Wall Street firms that upgraded Dell was CS First Boston, which raised the stock to 'buy' from 'hold'.
